advances: The proposed Boolean budget is false already at m=7: there are 93 distinct spike points and at least 37 Boolean points in their convex hull, so the complete lattice hull has at least 130 points, exceeding 128. A uniform four-point rational certificate proves membership for an explicit family in every dimension. This family also proves that the complete block size divided by 2^m tends to 2, rather than remaining at most 1. These assertions concern the single-block cardinality bridge and do not assert any halfspace-depth conclusion.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The matching description of the prescribed recursion, the four-spike rational witnesses, and the reflection count are proved here. Exact exploratory computations selected the witness mechanism but are not premises of the proof; no exclusion or numerical infeasibility claim is used.
proof:
First describe the standard successor directly on words. Scan a Boolean word from left to right, keeping a stack of previously unmatched zeros. A zero is pushed onto the stack. A one is paired with the last zero on the stack if the stack is nonempty; otherwise that one remains unmatched. At the end, all unmatched ones precede all unmatched zeros. Indeed, a zero that remains unmatched would have been available to any later unmatched one.

The matched pairs are noncrossing. More precisely, no unmatched position lies strictly between the endpoints of a matched pair. If an unmatched zero lay there, it would be above the paired zero on the stack when the closing one was read, preventing that pair. If an unmatched one lay there, the opening zero would still be on the stack when that one was read, preventing the one from being unmatched. Consequently the word consists of its unmatched symbols, separated by words all of whose symbols are matched internally. Each intervening word has equally many zeros and ones and has at least as many zeros as ones in each prefix. It therefore matches internally even if the unmatched symbols outside it are changed. Thus changing any selection of unmatched symbols leaves these intervening matches intact, and the remaining matching can be computed on the word of unmatched symbols alone.

For this matching, the standard recursive successor \(F_m\) is obtained by changing the first unmatched zero to one, and the word is terminal exactly when it has no unmatched zero. Here and below "first" refers to coordinate order. We prove this assertion by induction on dimension, including dimension zero with no successor. Changing the first unmatched zero in a reduced word \(1^p0^q\), where \(q>0\), changes its reduced word to \(1^{p+1}0^{q-1}\); the preceding internally matched words stay matched. Hence this operation removes exactly one unmatched zero.

Suppose the assertion holds in dimension \(m\). Appending zero to an old word preserves its old matching and adds a last unmatched zero. If the old word is nonterminal, its first unmatched zero remains the first one and its old successor edge appears with appended zero in the first new chain. If the old word is terminal, the new zero is its first unmatched zero, and the new edge is exactly the edge from the old terminal word with appended zero to the same word with appended one.

Appending one to an old word with at least one unmatched zero pairs that one with the last old unmatched zero. If at least two old unmatched zeros were present, the first one remains available. The old word and its old successor both precede the old terminal word, so the corresponding successor edge with appended one lies in the second new chain. If exactly one old unmatched zero was present, the old word was penultimate, and its copy with appended one is the terminal word of the second new chain. If no old unmatched zero was present, the copy with appended one is the terminal word of the first new chain. These exhaust the new words and exactly reproduce the stated recursion. This proves the successor rule.

Now fix a Boolean word \(b\) having at least three unmatched ones. Let \(j_1<j_2<j_3\) be the positions of its last three unmatched ones. Before modification, its unmatched-symbol word is \(1^p0^q\) with \(p\ge3\). Keep every other coordinate of \(b\) fixed, and replace its coordinates \(j_1,j_2,j_3\) by, respectively, the four patterns
$$
000,\qquad 100,\qquad 110,\qquad 010.
$$
Call these four source words \(c^{(1)},c^{(2)},c^{(3)},c^{(4)}\). The previously matched intervening words remain matched. On deleting them, the four remaining words are
$$
1^{p-3}0000^q,\qquad
1^{p-3}1000^q,\qquad
1^{p-3}1100^q,\qquad
1^{p-3}0100^q.
$$
In the fourth word the \(01\) at \(j_1,j_2\) matches, leaving \(j_3\) as the first unmatched zero. The first unmatched zeros in the four words therefore occur at \(j_1,j_2,j_3,j_3\), respectively. By the successor rule, all four sources lie in \(D_m\), and
$$
i_m(c^{(1)})=j_1,\quad
i_m(c^{(2)})=j_2,\quad
i_m(c^{(3)})=i_m(c^{(4)})=j_3.
$$
Their four spike points in \(E_m\) agree with \(b\) outside these three positions and have the respective patterns
$$
200,\qquad120,\qquad112,\qquad012.
$$
Their arithmetic mean is \(b\), since \((200+120+112+012)/4=111\) coordinate by coordinate. This is the promised exact rational certificate. It also applies when \(q>0\), so it does not require \(b\) to be terminal.

To identify how many words have at least three unmatched ones, let the walk associated to \(b\) have increments \(+1\) at ones and \(-1\) at zeros, and start at zero. During the matching scan, the number of unmatched ones increases exactly when a one is read with no unmatched zero available. These are exactly the steps at which the walk achieves a new maximum. Therefore its final number of unmatched ones equals
$$
\max_{0\le k\le m}\left(2\sum_{j=1}^k b_j-k\right).
$$
This proves the stated membership condition.

For completeness, count those words by reflection at their first visit to height 3. Reflecting all increments after that visit sends an ending height \(h\) to \(6-h\), and is an involution on paths visiting height 3.

For length \(2r\), every path ending at height at least 4 visits height 3. Reflection bijects the paths that visit height 3 and end at height at most 2 with all paths ending at height at least 4. A word with \(k\) ones has ending height \(2k-2r\), so
$$
N_{2r}=2\sum_{k=r+2}^{2r}\binom{2r}{k}
=2^{2r}-\binom{2r}{r}-2\binom{2r}{r+1}.
$$
For length \(2r+1\), the paths ending at height 3 number \(\binom{2r+1}{r+2}\), and those ending at height at least 5 number \(\sum_{k=r+3}^{2r+1}\binom{2r+1}{k}\). Reflection bijects paths visiting height 3 and ending at height at most 1 with paths ending at height at least 5. Thus
$$
\begin{aligned}
N_{2r+1}
&=\binom{2r+1}{r+2}
+2\sum_{k=r+3}^{2r+1}\binom{2r+1}{k}\\
&=2^{2r+1}-2\binom{2r+1}{r+1}
-\binom{2r+1}{r+2}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The empty-sum convention covers \(r=0\). These are counts of an explicit certified family, rather than numerical hull-membership counts.

Every point of \(E_m\) has exactly one coordinate equal to 2 and all other coordinates Boolean. The convex-realization lemma in accepted fact 032423921efad6c8, applied to this new set \(E_m\), gives \(\operatorname{conv}(B_m\cup E_m)\cap\mathbb Z^m=B_m\cup E_m\). Since \(\operatorname{conv}(E_m)\) is contained in that hull, every point of \(T_m\) is either in \(E_m\) or Boolean. Both reverse inclusions hold by definition, proving the disjoint union \(T_m=E_m\mathbin{\dot\cup}C_m^{\mathrm{bool}}\).

The spike map is injective: its unique coordinate equal to 2 identifies the selected coordinate, and changing that entry back to zero recovers its source. The chain count in accepted fact 032423921efad6c8 therefore gives \(|E_m|=|D_m|=2^m-\binom m{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\). Combining the certified family with the disjoint union proves the lower bound for \(|T_m|\). The trivial inclusion \(C_m^{\mathrm{bool}}\subseteq B_m\) proves the upper bound.

At \(m=7\), the exact walk count is
$$
N_7=2^7-2\binom74-\binom75=128-70-21=37.
$$
The 37 distinct words counted here each have the explicit four-spike certificate above. They are disjoint from the 93 distinct points of \(E_7\), since the latter each have a coordinate equal to 2. Hence \(|T_7|\ge93+37=130>128\), refuting the proposed all-dimension bound.

Finally, every binomial coefficient subtracted in either formula for \(N_m\) is at most \(\binom m{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\). Thus
$$
2^{m+1}-4\binom m{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}
\le |T_m|
\le2^{m+1}-\binom m{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}.
$$
The central binomial coefficient divided by \(2^m\) tends to zero. One elementary verification, also available in accepted fact 032423921efad6c8, is
$$
\frac{\binom{2r}{r}}{4^r}
=\prod_{h=1}^{r}\left(1-\frac1{2h}\right)
\le \exp\left(-\frac12\sum_{h=1}^{r}\frac1h\right)
\le \frac1{\sqrt{r+1}}
\quad(r\ge1).
$$
For odd dimension, \(\binom{2r+1}{r}/2^{2r+1}=\frac{2r+1}{2r+2}\binom{2r}{r}/4^r\), so the same conclusion holds. Divide the last two-sided bound by \(2^m\) to obtain \(|T_m|/2^m\to2\).
statement:
Use the Boolean cube \(B_m=\{0,1\}^m\), the nonterminal set \(D_m\), and the successor \(F_m(c)=c+e_{i_m(c)}\) from accepted fact 032423921efad6c8. Fix precisely its standard recursive chain partition: begin with the one empty chain in dimension zero, and replace each chain \(S_k,\ldots,S_{m-k}\) by
$$
\begin{aligned}
&S_k,\ldots,S_{m-k},S_{m-k}\cup\{m+1\},\\
&S_k\cup\{m+1\},\ldots,S_{m-k-1}\cup\{m+1\},
\end{aligned}
$$
omitting an empty second chain. Introduce the new block objects \(E_m=\{c+2e_{i_m(c)}:c\in D_m\}\), \(T_m=\operatorname{conv}(E_m)\cap\mathbb Z^m\), and \(C_m^{\mathrm{bool}}=\operatorname{conv}(E_m)\cap B_m\).

For every \(m\ge1\) and \(b\in B_m\), the condition
$$
\max_{0\le k\le m}\left(2\sum_{j=1}^k b_j-k\right)\ge3
$$
implies \(b\in C_m^{\mathrm{bool}}\). Every such membership has a convex-combination certificate consisting of four points of \(E_m\), each with coefficient \(1/4\), specified in the proof.

Let \(N_m\) denote the number of Boolean words satisfying this condition. With binomial coefficients outside their usual range interpreted as zero, their exact counts are
$$
\begin{aligned}
N_{2r}&=2^{2r}-\binom{2r}{r}-2\binom{2r}{r+1}
&& (r\ge1),\\
N_{2r+1}&=2^{2r+1}-2\binom{2r+1}{r+1}
-\binom{2r+1}{r+2}
&& (r\ge0).
\end{aligned}
$$
Furthermore,
$$
T_m=E_m\mathbin{\dot\cup}C_m^{\mathrm{bool}},
\qquad
2^m-\binom m{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}+N_m
\le |T_m|
\le 2^{m+1}-\binom m{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}.
$$
In particular \(N_7=37\), \(|T_7|\ge130>2^7\), and \(\lim_{m\to\infty}|T_m|/2^m=2\). No assertion that the displayed Boolean family exhausts \(C_m^{\mathrm{bool}}\) is needed.
